beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW - Claude UI cold open. The prompt is an ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION of the walker ask, never a transcript.
beats.narration_text: Sawubona, this is Liam, in for Bear. The ask, reconstructed: in Mimic Keep, an archer on a castle wall shoots fire arrows at straw scarecrows. Add two particle effects: one says an arrow hit, one says a scarecrow is still burning, and how long it has left.

props.command: Please use Walker to add two GPU particle effects to Mimic Keep, my castle-defense game where an archer on the wall shoots fire arrows at straw scarecrows: a one-shot impact burst on every arrow hit, and burning embers whose density follows each scarecrow's remaining burn time. I write the brief, the predictions and every verdict; agents build, wire and test; I judge the look in the running game.

beats.role_note: What was built, with one real correction: the fixture strips cannot show the hit-on-burning overlap.
beats.narration_text: Two effects, specified by Rui, built and wired by agent sessions, and tuned twice by Rui's eyes. The tests can read every node, and see no particle. The fixture strips see particles, but no hit. So the overlap Rui found was only visible in the running game.

props.text:
Mimic Keep:

beats.role_note: The game and both effects in play.
beats.narration_text: This is the game, running with nobody at the keys. The archer fires on its own. Every hit throws a flash and straw. Every fire hit sets a scarecrow burning for four seconds, and embers rise from it, thinning as the burn runs out.

shot.label: Scarecrows placed by the script · no keys pressed

qc.full_bleed_reason: Native 3840x2160 engine capture fills the frame by design.
qc.contrast_reason: Engine footage of a flat green meadow by design; the text a viewer must read is the burned-in label, so contrast is measured there.

beats.role_note: The brief's two jobs, event and condition, before any code.
beats.narration_text: Rui wrote the brief first. Effect A answers an event: an accepted hit, through a new signal, hit taken, the one gameplay change the brief allows. Effect B answers a condition: burn time left, read every frame, because a second fire hit refreshes the burn without any signal.

props.title: Two jobs, one event, one condition
props.status: WRITTEN BY RUI BEFORE ANY BUILD · 2026-11-05

cards.label: Effect A · event
cards.text: every accepted Scarecrow.hit() emits hit_taken(position) → one new burst

cards.label: Retrigger rule
cards.text: overlap: a new instance per hit, up to 3 alive, never reused

cards.label: Effect B · condition
cards.text: burn_time_left 4 → 0 s drives amount_ratio 1 → 0 on each scarecrow

cards.label: Node type
cards.text: GPUParticles2D for both: CPUParticles2D has no amount_ratio, no turbulence

beats.role_note: Effect A's intent block: timing, contrast, scale, change over life.
beats.narration_text: Effect A's intent block. A sharp yellow white flash at the hit point, about eight frames, smaller than the scarecrow's head. Straw fragments fly out, fall, darken and fade within point eight seconds, so they can overlap the next hit, but never a third.

props.title: Effect A · Arrow Impact Burst
props.excerpt: The flash communicates the exact moment of impact; the fragments provide a short visible aftermath.

cards.label: Timing
cards.text: flash 0.28 s (≈ 8 frames at 30 fps) · straw 0.80 s

cards.label: Contrast
cards.text: bright flash on grass and gate · dark straw on wall and walkway

cards.label: Scale
cards.text: flash smaller than the head · straw about the scarecrow's width

cards.label: Change over life
cards.text: flash: small → wider → orange → gone · straw: out, fall, darken, fade

beats.role_note: The three parts of a particle system, each tied to a line of the effect's scene file.
beats.narration_text: Every particle system has three parts. The emitter decides how many particles and for how long. The process material moves each one: velocity, gravity, colour over life. The draw step decides what each particle looks like: here a soft dot, added as light.

props.title: Three parts of a particle system.
props.source: Verbatim project source at commit 3b99ea6 · Godot editor reconstruction (teaching view)
props.code:
[node name="Flash" type="GPUParticles2D" parent="."]
material = SubResource("CanvasItemMaterial_flash")
emitting = false
amount = 10
texture = ExtResource("1_dot")
lifetime = 0.28
one_shot = true
preprocess = 0.0
explosiveness = 1.0
local_coords = false
visibility_rect = Rect2(-64, -64, 128, 128)
process_material = SubResource("ParticleProcessMaterial_flash")

beats.role_note: Effect A's first strip and Rui's first verdict.
beats.narration_text: The first strip, from a preview fixture with a fixed seed. Rui looked first, and wrote that during the flash the straw could not be seen. The strip agreed, and showed why: the straw's first colour equals the scarecrow's body.

shot.label: Fixture capture · preview scene, fixed seed

beats.role_note: Effect A revision r1: observation, prediction, before and after, verdict.
beats.narration_text: Revision one. In the running game Rui saw the flash start a little bright, and asked for it darker. The agent predicted a softer flash. The after strip dimmed it on the grass, but barely on the burning body, where added light was already clipped at full yellow. Rui kept it: in play, the straw read better.

beats.role_note: Effect A in play, including rapid repeats.
beats.narration_text: In play: hits from near and far land close together, so bursts overlap. The state test fired real arrows, measured three bursts alive at the third impact, and every one freed itself after its lifetime.

beats.role_note: Effect B's intent, the feature Effect A doesn't use, start/stop/pause behaviour.
beats.narration_text: Effect B's intent. Embers rise from the body, pale yellow to orange red, over faint smoke. It uses two things Effect A doesn't: amount ratio, so density follows the burn, and turbulence on the smoke. When the scarecrow dies, the embers move to the effects layer and fade.

props.title: Effect B · Burning Embers
props.excerpt: Smoke also uses mild turbulence so that it does not rise in identical straight lines.

cards.label: Timing
cards.text: 0.5 s to the head · stream full after 0.9 s · tail ≤ 1.2 s

cards.label: Start / stop
cards.text: burning_started → on, ratio 1 · burning_ended → off, ratio 0

cards.label: Pause / death
cards.text: paused: frozen · died: stop, move to World/Effects, free after 1.2 s

beats.role_note: The feedback driver, verbatim.
beats.narration_text: The driver reads burn time left every frame and turns it into amount ratio, never amount. A refresh needs no signal: the next frame reads four seconds and the density jumps back to full.

beats.role_note: Effect B's first strip and Rui's first verdict.
beats.narration_text: Effect B's first strip. Rui watched first: the weakening was hard to notice. The strip's counts follow the brief, ten, six, four, three, but most embers sit on the yellow burning body, where added light clips.

shot.label: Fixture capture · preview scene, fixed seed

beats.role_note: Effect B revision r1: observation, prediction, before and after, verdict.
beats.narration_text: Revision one for B came from the game: Rui saw the hit flash and the embers merge. The agent traced it to a shared texture, blend and colour, and made new embers fade in over the flash's time. The strip changed less than predicted, for the same clipping reason. Rui kept it: now the two read a little apart.

beats.role_note: Effect B start, refresh, pause, burn-out and death.
beats.narration_text: Start, refresh, pause and death, scripted on the real game. A fire hit starts the embers. A second hit refreshes them to full. Escape freezes them. They thin as the burn runs down, and a scarecrow that dies while burning leaves its embers behind to fade.

beats.narration_text: Rui converted the flash's process material into code. Line three sixteen starts the force as gravity, the brief's zero, one hundred. Line three twenty nine adds force times delta to the velocity. Texture and blend are not in here: they belong to drawing.

beats.role_note: Tests, mutations, both prices against budget, the headless limit.
beats.narration_text: What the tests proved: every setting read back, every trigger and condition driven by real arrows and keys. Four mutations failed them, including a silent Godot three name. A GPU effect's headless price is near zero by design: the dummy renderer runs no particle work. On the real GPU, both stayed far under budget.

shot.label: Recorded output · test logs and cost script

beats.role_note: Agent mistakes caught, Claude's readings overruled, what remains uncertain.
beats.narration_text: Mistakes caught. The agent's preview had no fixed seed, and its capture path was wrong twice. Claude's first rectangle check used swapped screenshots, and was withdrawn. Rui overruled one strip reading: the strip said the straw was no clearer, the game said it was. Still uncertain: a hidden emitter paused, against Rui's prediction.

beats.role_note: Your Turn - a paste-ready Walker prompt; Liam signs off here, before the final card.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the paste ready prompt. Give one event and one condition an effect each. Write the intent and the predicted strip before the build. Let an agent build and test it, then watch it in the game yourself, because the strip can't see what play does. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Use Walker. Pick one event and one condition in my game. I will write each effect's intent, settings and predicted frame strip before anything is built. Build each as a GPUParticles2D scene with a configuration test, wire it with a state test driven by real input, and give me a fixed-seed preview to capture. I judge every tuning change in the running game.
